name: DuPont

summary.text: DuPont de Nemours, Inc. is the specialty products company that remained after DowDuPont separated into three publicly traded companies in 2019: Dow (materials science) on 1 April 2019 and Corteva (agriculture) on 1 June 2019. The historical DuPont was a member of the Global Climate Coalition. In the NPR and FRONTLINE investigation 'Plastic Wars', former DuPont manager Ronald Liesemer described being assigned to carry out the plastics industry's recycling promotion from the late 1980s, at a time when industry documents from the 1970s had expressed doubt that recycling was economically viable. In 2023 DuPont, Chemours and Corteva agreed to pay $1.185 billion to settle PFAS drinking-water claims by a class of U.S. public water systems; the U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina approved the settlement in February 2024.

facts.claim: DowDuPont separated into three companies in 2019. Dow Inc. was spun off on 1 April 2019 through a pro rata dividend of one Dow share for every three DowDuPont shares; Corteva, Inc., holding the agriculture business, was separated on 1 June 2019; the remaining company, holding specialty products, was renamed DuPont de Nemours, Inc.
facts.quote: A Dow Inc. filing says the separation of Dow occurred on April 1, 2019.

sources.title: DowDuPont Spins Off Corteva and Relaunches as the New DuPont

facts.claim: In June 2023 Chemours, DuPont and Corteva announced an agreement in principle to resolve PFAS drinking-water claims by a class of U.S. public water systems through a $1.185 billion settlement fund, with Chemours contributing about $592 million, DuPont about $400 million and Corteva about $193 million under a January 2021 cost-sharing memorandum. Personal injury claims and state attorney-general natural resource claims were excluded, and the companies denied the allegations.
facts.quote: The companies will collectively establish and contribute a total of $1.185 billion to a settlement fund ("water district settlement fund").

sources.title: Chemours, DuPont and Corteva Reach Comprehensive PFAS Settlement with U.S. Water Systems
Chemours, DuPont and Corteva Reach Comprehensive PFAS Settlement with U.S. Water Systems

facts.claim: In February 2024 Judge Richard Gergel of the U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina approved the $1.185 billion PFAS class settlement between DuPont, Chemours, Corteva and public water systems, finding the class settlement fair.
facts.quote: Judge Gergel found that a class action is the best way to settle the case and that the settlement between water utilities and the chemical companies is fair.

facts.claim: The 2020 NPR and FRONTLINE investigation 'Plastic Wars' reported that plastics industry documents from the 1970s, including an April 1973 report to senior executives, called recycling costly and difficult and described sorting as infeasible, and that a 1974 document expressed serious doubt about its economic viability. From the late 1980s the industry spent tens of millions of dollars promoting recycling. Former DuPont manager Ronald Liesemer described being assigned to carry out that recycling push, which former industry officials said was used to head off proposed plastic bans.
facts.quote: Starting in the late 1980s, the plastics industry spent tens of millions of dollars promoting recycling through ads, recycling projects and public relations.

facts.claim: An October 2010 ETC Group report identified 262 patent families, covering 1,663 patent documents published between June 2008 and June 2010, claiming environmental stress tolerance in plants. It found that DuPont, Monsanto, BASF, Bayer, Syngenta and their partners accounted for 77% of the families and that DuPont, BASF and Monsanto alone accounted for over two-thirds. ETC Group is an advocacy organisation and the counts were not independently verified.
facts.quote: The same report found that just three companies – DuPont, BASF, Monsanto – account for over two-thirds of the total.

connections.claim: DuPont was a member of the Global Climate Coalition, the industry group that opposed the Kyoto Protocol and disbanded in 2002.
connections.quote: Other prominent members included BP, Royal Dutch Shell, DuPont, Ford Motor Company, Daimler Chrysler, Texaco, General Motors, and Exxon.

connections.claim: Dow and DuPont were combined as DowDuPont and then separated: Dow Inc. was spun off on 1 April 2019 and the remaining company became DuPont de Nemours after Corteva's separation on 1 June 2019.
connections.quote: Dow stockholders received shares through a pro rata dividend, with one share of Dow common stock for every three shares of DowDuPont common stock held.

sources.title: DowDuPont Spins Off Corteva and Relaunches as the New DuPont

connections.claim: DuPont, Chemours and Corteva jointly settled PFAS drinking-water claims by U.S. public water systems for $1.185 billion, sharing the cost under a January 2021 memorandum of understanding; the court approved the settlement in February 2024.
connections.quote: Contribution rates will be consistent with the binding Memorandum of Understanding between the companies reached in January 2021, with Chemours contributing 50 percent (about $592 million), and DuPont (about $400 million) and Corteva (about $193 million) collectively contributing the remaining 50 percent.

openQuestions: The 1973 and 1974 plastics-industry documents cited in 'Plastic Wars' are not attributed to DuPont in the coverage found; the full investigation should be checked for their authorship.
The site's Crash Conduits entry on DuPont, General Motors and the 1934 Business Plot was outside the scope of this climate-focused research.
The Corteva separation date of 1 June 2019 is stated as planned in the filings found; the completion should be confirmed in Corteva's 2019 Form 8-K.
